transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I'm here because... well, I realized recently that I keep arranging my entire house and my daily routine around not seeing spiders. Which is exhausting. I live in this lovely older craftsman place, you see, which I bought about ten years ago when I started teaching at the secondary school. The architecture is just gorgeous, all original woodwork, but older houses definitely have their quirks. The draftiness in the winter is just dreadful, honestly. I had to buy three space heaters last November just to sit and grade papers in the living room without freezing. 

But anyway, the spiders... I literally put off doing my laundry for days on end because the machine is down in the basement. And the garden shed? I completely avoid it. Which is a real shame because I absolutely love gardening. My hydrangeas were beautiful last spring. The soil around our neighborhood is perfect for them, very acidic, which makes the blooms that deep, vibrant blue... 

But yes, I actually end up paying people to do small jobs out there, or down in the basement. Handymen, the neighbor's boy... I pay them to do things I know perfectly well how to do myself, just because I can’t make myself go into those spaces. I just can't do it.
Are there other places or things you avoid besides the basement and garden shed because of your fear of spiders?

Well, let me think... not really, no. I mean, the basement and the shed are the main ones because they're so dark and, you know, undisturbed. Spiders just love those undisturbed spaces. Actually, that reminds me of when I was cleaning out my classroom over the summer. I teach history, mostly European history for the upperclassmen, and I have these massive filing cabinets full of old maps and primary source documents. Some of those documents are copies I made fifteen years ago, back when we still used those awful overhead projectors. Do you remember those? The clear plastic sheets you had to write on with those special markers that always got on your hands? It was just a nightmare trying to keep them organized. 

Anyway, I was pulling out this stack of old French Revolution materials—I always do a big unit on the French Revolution, the kids love the drama of it all, Marie Antoinette and the guillotine, you know—and I just had this sudden panic that there might be something behind the cabinet. But no, it's really just the basement and the shed at home that I completely avoid. I try to keep the rest of the house very clean, very bright, so they don't have anywhere to hide.
